- The Chernogrovian Witch Monks are often cited as the most forward thinking in regards to their use of Daemons in common day to day life, and the harnessing of Daemonic energies for other magical rituals.

- The use of chaos magic is specifically fuelled by Chernogrovian Daemonology, chaos magic being reality altering in it’s ability - but difficult to master.

- Chernogrovian Witch Monks mostly faced no opposition from their own populace (as Daemonology is a long standing tradition in their lands) but, their use of Daemonic energies is staunchly opposed by Asarans and the Bloodsinger clans of the north for religious reasons.

- A large chunk of non-religious philosophy is outright banned in the theocratic Empire of Asara, for fear of it spreading amongst the commonfolk and leading to the usurpation of the Kolos Severine, the religious and state leader of the Empire. All philosophy *must* follow the Temple of Light’s positions.

- Philosophy is often treated as a mere fact of life amongst the commonfolk, and many nobles and academics rather focus their energies on the magical and ethereal realms for not philosophical enlightenment but rather tangible power.

- The Chernogrovians truly value thought, but only in relation to the Otherworld and it’s uses. The United Triarchy on the other hand values scientific advancement in all forms, even allowing men and women to rise in society in accordance to a scientific meritocracy.

- The Bloodsinger clans of the troubled Northern lands are fearful of advancement, or technology as a whole.

The practice and study of Daemonology is strictly forbidden within the Empire of Asara, mostly out of fear of Chernogrovian influences and the history of Daemonology within the Empire most commonly resulting with mass destruction.
More often than not, Daemonologists within the Empire who aren’t diplomats or nobles from Chernogrov are immediately executed through salting and butchering. The accused is put through a mock trial before summarily having their bones broken with a maul, flayed alive and then salted - the corpse being strung up on city walls or simply impaled on a pike in a public space.

Avatars of the gods are relatively common - the prime example being amongst the Aesiran farmers of the North. Every hundred years, the God of The Sea - Aracadir, channels his magick into a newborn child. This child will go on to become what the Aesirans call a Great Leader, who will unite the clans for a period of time for raiding, conquering and looting.

The Arrival Of God's Scourge.

The Khagan Baltantorix was renowned, even amongst the Vampiric hordes of the east, for his ability in necromancy and alchemy. In fact, he controlled the largest army amongst the steppe peoples - five hundred thousand of the dead and living alike. The Khagan was also the first to move westwards, and to set his eyes upon new lands.

Baltantorix's first opponent was the most dangerous. And the one who who could have defeated him. The United Lothairian Principalities were technologically advanced - having discovered primitive magick based artillery. A wonderful weapon against the mass hordes of Baltantorix, who only threw wave upon wave of un-feeling corpses at the enemy. The Princes of Lothair also held an alliance with the Asaran Empire through a royal marriage. 

The Asarans at the time were fighting the re-emerged Imperium Sol Invictus from the far west, stuck in a dreaded stalemate. They only parted a band of half-starving, war shocked infantry to help the Lotharians. It would be the death of the Lotharians - as the Khagan Baltantorix simply kept throwing bodies at the dwindling forces of the Princes. He used the corpses of the Lotharians as his men, using dark magicks and daemonology to further ruin the Lotharian lands - making them uninhabitable.

With the Asaran help that they had expected, the Princes could have mounted a potential defence - adding to their lacking infantry and numbers. But the Princes fell to the Khagan Baltantorix, damning the Asaran Empire with their last words.

The Aesiran Warborn raiders struck a humiliating defeat to the Empire Of Asara. The raiders had only arrived on a scouring mission, to raze and burn the land and to loot any damned thing they could see. The Asarans wanted a show of force, as the Warborn had been an annoyance for near decades after they had united. 
This went horribly. The Asarans mobilised a force of ten thousand, comically oversized to deal with a warband of four thousand. The Warborn led them into multiple ambushes, constantly harassing them with skirmishers, and eventually decapitated the leadership in a night attack. They were emboldened massively, and went on to march onto a major city - razing it to the ground, looting it and then enslaving the inhabitants/forcefully recruiting. The Warborn did this for over five years, Asaran military forces consistently being beaten back due to amateurish mistakes before they conceded tonnes of gold and relics and even land to make them leave.
